I think it's helpful for those thinking how to implement this (unless, you'd like to give it a try), if you provide some more detail. 

For example: 
1. How would you implement this? If you don't know how you would do it programmatically, you could describe the "high-level" vision of how this would work. For example, as a Calendso user you can currently create different event types of various durations — you can then decide which event type to send the link to. Thus, would you have a completely separate "customisable duration event type", which is the only event type that for which duration can be changed? What's your vision?
2. I might be misunderstanding what you are saying, but an "inviter" is the person inviting, and "invitee" is the person being invited — if you send your Calendso link to someone, then you are the inviter, and the person you are sending it to, an invitee. Therefore, by saying "[I want to] let the inviter set the meeting duration/ending time" - do you mean "invitee"? Since you can already can do that as an inviter (the person sending the invite) — you create different event types as a Calendso user and thus implicitly set the duration of those events when creating an event type and sending off the link. 

Apologies if misunderstood what you said but if you can clarify then I can start thinking about the ways in which this could be accomplished and perhaps ask you for some additional clarification. 
--

I like this idea. I'm not sure if Calendly has this feature.

From a UX perspective, here's how I think it would work:
1. For a specific or every Friday, 1pm-5pm are my 1:1 "office hours" for my students (invitees). I select that they can schedule a block of 15, 30 or 60 minutes depending on their need (I would think these 3 would be the top 3 options available and in demand, with 20 min and 50 min being the 2 other timeframes that I would recommend being options for the inviter's UI)
2. Invitee goes to meeting booking screen in Calendso, select the date of interest
3. Here's where the UI would differ: Invitee is asked if they'd like a 15, 30, or 60 minute meeting
4. the UI provides meeting start times at 15 minute intervals such that the 15, 30, or 60 minute meeting would end within the 1-5pm time frame
5. Same UI moving forward for booking meetings as with regular meeting.

Future features: ability for invitee to return to start of booking process if invitee wants to change the meeting duration to longer or shorter.

Let me know if I'm misinterpreting this.

> have an event type for 15min, 30min and one for 60min (that's how all scheduling tools do it)

Unfortunately this is not a good solution.  I already tried that as a workaround in the past, and it was a massive pain.  For example, let's say I want the following event types:

- Personal video call for non-work topics
- In-person meeting for personal topics
- Work video call with colleagues within my company
- Work video call with external particpants outside my company

All of these need their own event type, because they all require different parameters.  However I want to give anyone requesting any of these types of meetings a choice of different time durations.  (The "office hours" scenario mentioned above is one of several great reasons why this can be needed.)  If those choices are limited to, say, 30 / 60 / 90 mins, then that multiplies the four event types above by 3, so I have to create 12 event types in total.  If I also want to allow other durations like 15 mins or 120 mins then it gets even worse.

> in my experience its quite rare that the same event type has different durations.

I can of course appreciate that this is your experience, but it doesn't mean that many other people have different needs.  If you want to cater to the huge addressable market for calendar apps then I believe this is the kind of flexibility a lot of people will find useful. 

So I would be super grateful if you could reconsider this feature request.  I know that some of your competitors don't offer this feature, but that's a great opportunity for Cal to differentiate itself and become even more awesome ;-)
--

[**@PeerRich**](https://github.com/PeerRich) commented on [March 19, 2022 11:39 PM](https://github.com/calcom/cal.com/issues/88#issuecomment-1073130620 "2022-03-19T23:39:59Z - Replied by Github Reply Comments"):
> can you recommend your favorite way you'd want this to be implemented?

Thanks a lot for the quick response and for being open-minded on this!  I think the implementation could be very simple:

1. When creating a new event type, multiple durations are allowed, e.g. add a `+` (plus) icon to add extra durations, and a trash icon to remove them.  Or allow comma-separated values like `15,30,60` as a more quick and dirty implementation.
2. When using an event type link to book a slot, if the event type has multiple durations, then the person booking the event has to first choose a duration before proceeding as normal with the rest of the booking process.  Then the availability will be displayed according to that chosen event duration.
3. Make it easy (i.e. ideally with a single click) for the person booking to change their duration choice after selection, in which case the displayed availability is adjusted accordingly. So for example if they are looking for an hour slot but can't find any availability which works for them, they have the option of reducing the slot to 30 mins in order to potentially gain more options.
4. [Stretch goal for optimal UX] If the event type allows multiple durations, then after the user of the link selects a duration and a day, if there are no slots available for that combination, do one of the following:
    - If there are smaller slots available on that day, rather than just displaying "All booked today", display something like "No 60 minute slots today, but there are two 30 minute slots." and a button "__Reduce duration to 30 minutes__" which changes the duration parameter and updates the display accordingly.
    - If there are *no* smaller slots available on that day, display something like "No slots of any duration available today".  (Just keeping the original "All booked today" text would also be OK, but I was thinking that this change might clarify the situation a bit better in this case.)

I also note that there seems to be some terminology confusion here which we should try to clear up:

[**@harad**](https://github.com/harad) commented on [April 22, 2021 9:43 PM](https://github.com/calcom/cal.com/issues/88#issuecomment-825172079 "2021-04-22T20:43:30Z - Replied by Github Reply Comments"):
> 2.  I might be misunderstanding what you are saying, but an "inviter" is the person inviting, and "invitee" is the person being invited — if you send your Calendso link to someone, then you are the inviter, and the person you are sending it to, an invitee.

That seems the exact opposite of what I'd expect, and therefore quite confusing.  In my mind, the person who receives the link and uses it to request a meeting is the one trying to set up the meeting, and therefore they are the inviter, and the owner of the cal.com account and link is the invitee.  In other words, "I am using your cal.com link to invite you to a meeting".

Perhaps this confusion stems from the fact that an event link can either result in an immediate booking, or it can result in an invite which requires confirmation.  In the former case, I can see an argument for describing the link sender (i.e. cal.com account holder) as the "inviter", since they are inviting the counterparty to book their time.  But in the latter case, the link sender is "inviting the other party to create an invite"!

> Therefore, by saying "\[I want to\] let the inviter set the meeting duration/ending time" - do you mean "invitee"? Since you can already can do that as an inviter (the person sending the invite) — you create different event types as a Calendso user and thus implicitly set the duration of those events when creating an event type and sending off the link.

Since the original description begins with the words "As a Calendso user who is invited to meet with the inviter", it seems very clear to me that this is not what is being asked for, and that @kimjin8 and I both think of the Calendso user being the "invitee" and the person using the link as the "inviter".  It is well understood that an event type can already be customised to a single, fixed duration, but this issue is requesting more than that, i.e. that the duration of the event type can be flexible.
--

It is well understood that an event type can already be customised to a single, fixed duration, but this issue is requesting more than that, i.e. that the duration of the event type can be flexible.

@aspiers whilst I appreciate your argument, I still think that the cal.com's user is the inviter, and the person receiving the link would be the invitee. Since the link originates with the inviter, not the invitee. Ultimately, it's the person with the greater control over the link and the available times for the meeting should be the inviter. 

The inviter, the cal.com's user, is streamlining the process of scheduling a meeting with them, and therefore, makes a link available. Interesting take on: 'In other words, "I am using your cal.com link to invite you to a meeting"'. - I would argue it's the right opposite, and your example is very specific. Whilst it's true in some cases and probably largely depends on the way you use cal.com, I use cal.com to simply reduce back-and-forth, even when I'm the one asking the person for a meeting - therefore, for me, it'd be more of "I am asking you to use my cal.com link to invite you to a meeting". As in, I am providing you with my cal.com link, so we can have a meeting at a mutually convenient time. If you send a birthday party invitation, who is the inviter, and who is the invitee? The person whose birthday we are celebrating, or the person who is attending the party? I'd strongly argue it's the former, not the latter. 

Whilst I don't have the data to back it up to what most people think - I think potentially changing the meaning of inviter/invitee could lead to some serious confusion among the users. Happy to be proved wrong.  
--

Thanks @harad, I do see your points.  Ultimately both perspectives have validity, and it's not a matter of one being right and the other being wrong.  In case you have any doubts about that, please consider this scenario:

1. I have a conversation with a friend or colleague, either online or offline, in which I mention that if they ever need to talk to me about anything, they are welcome to book a time slot via the given cal.com URL.  They make a note of this URL for future use.
2. Six months later, they visit this URL to book a time slot.  An email automatically appears in my inbox asking me to confirm whether I am OK with that time slot.  I confirm, and the meeting happens.
3. Six months later, the same thing happens again.

In this scenario, they are much closer to being the inviter than I am, since I never requested organisation of a specific event; I merely expressed my openness to being available, should they wish to meet with me.  On both occasions, they were the one who initially proposed the meeting.  Cal.com was merely the tool to facilitate this process in an efficient manner, but I could have equally said "look, if you ever want to talk, just send me an email and we'll find a time we're both free".

But anyway, let's not get too distracted into a long debate on the semantics ;-) That would not be very productive, and it's certainly off topic for this particular GitHub issue.  There are two concrete takeaways here:

1. It seems very clear that the OP was using "inviter" to refer to the person using the link to book a time slot.
2. As a more general point, it's important that cal.com uses clear wording to avoid any confusion along these lines.  I believe the wording I have seen so far has been perfectly clear, so I'm not aware of anything actionable on that front.
--

/**
 * Builds a public booking page link for the same event type, prefilled with a previous attendee.
 * Shared by the "Book again" booking action and the People view.
 * @returns The relative booking link, or null when the event type can no longer be booked by link
 */
export function buildBookAgainUrl({
  eventType,
  username,
  attendee,
}: {
  eventType: { slug?: string | null; team?: { slug?: string | null } | null } | null | undefined;
  username?: string | null;
  attendee: { name: string; email: string };
}): string | null {
  const slug = eventType?.slug;
  if (!slug) return null;

  const teamSlug = eventType.team?.slug;
  let basePath: string;
  if (teamSlug) {
    basePath = `/team/${teamSlug}/${slug}`;
  } else if (username) {
    basePath = `/${username}/${slug}`;
  } else {
    return null;
  }

  const urlSearchParams = new URLSearchParams({ name: attendee.name, email: attendee.email });
  return `${basePath}?${urlSearchParams.toString()}`;
}

I've read issue #88 and the PR it depends on. Here's a summary and a proposed plan.

## Issue #88: Create the "People" view for easy rebooking
On CSCI-435-SE/cal.diy, assigned to you, sub-issue of #51. The upstream `calcom/cal.diy#88` is an unrelated closed issue, so I'm ignoring it.

**Goal:** a People view built from your past bookings. Each attendee shows up once with:
- name and email
- how many times you've met
- the date of your most recent meeting
- a **Book Again** action

It also needs an empty state and tests.

**Out of scope:** a contacts or address-book system, adding people by hand, editing attendee info, and any change to reschedule behavior.

**Dependency:** "Book Again" has to reuse the rebooking code from #87, which is PR #94 (`feat/issue-87-book-again`). That PR is open and not merged yet. It adds `apps/web/modules/bookings/lib/buildBookAgainUrl.ts`, and that file's doc comment already says it's shared with the People view. So #88 should branch from #94's branch, or wait for it to merge.

## Proposed plan (about 6–8 files, under 500 lines)
1. **Repository:** add a method on the attendee or booking repository that groups attendees of the user's past bookings by email in SQL (`groupBy`/aggregate with `select`). It returns the count and `max(endTime)`, plus the latest booking's event type slug, team slug and username so the Book Again URL can be built. Grouping in the database keeps it fast and avoids pulling every booking into memory.
2. **Service:** add a thin service that maps the rows to a `PersonDto` (name, email, meetingCount, lastMeetingAt, bookAgainUrl).
3. **tRPC:** add a `viewer.bookings.people` (or similar) query handler.
4. **UI:** add a People page under the bookings area (the main nav, or a tab next to Upcoming/Past). It uses a table or list, `buildBookAgainUrl` for the action, and an `EmptyScreen` when there's no one to show.
5. **i18n:** add the new strings to `packages/i18n/locales/en/common.json`.
6. **Tests:** cover grouping and deduplication, meeting counts, most-recent date, Book Again URL building, and the empty state.

Before I start, I need three decisions from you:
- **Base branch:** should I build on `feat/issue-87-book-again` (my recommendation) or wait until #94 merges?
- **Where People lives:** a new tab in the bookings list (the smallest change), or a separate sidebar page?
- **What counts as a "previous meeting":** I'd suggest only past bookings that were accepted, leaving out cancelled and rejected ones.

I'll make the edits and leave committing to you, as usual.

import { getServerSession } from "@calcom/features/auth/lib/getServerSession";
import { FeaturesRepository } from "@calcom/features/flags/features.repository";
import { prisma } from "@calcom/prisma";
import { buildLegacyRequest } from "@lib/buildLegacyCtx";
import type { PageProps } from "app/_types";
import { _generateMetadata, getTranslate } from "app/_utils";
import { ShellMainAppDir } from "app/(use-page-wrapper)/(main-nav)/ShellMainAppDir";
import { cookies, headers } from "next/headers";
import { redirect } from "next/navigation";
import { z } from "zod";
import { validStatuses } from "~/bookings/lib/validStatuses";
import BookingsList from "~/bookings/views/bookings-view";

const querySchema = z.object({
  status: z.enum(validStatuses),
});

export const generateMetadata = async ({ params }: { params: Promise<{ status: string }> }) =>
  await _generateMetadata(
    (t) => t("bookings"),
    (t) => t("bookings_description"),
    undefined,
    undefined,
    `/bookings/${(await params).status}`
  );

const Page = async ({ params }: PageProps) => {
  const parsed = querySchema.safeParse(await params);
  if (!parsed.success) {
    redirect("/bookings/upcoming");
  }
  const t = await getTranslate();
  const session = await getServerSession({ req: buildLegacyRequest(await headers(), await cookies()) });

  if (!session?.user?.id) {
    return redirect("/auth/login");
  }

  const userId = session.user.id;
  const featuresRepository = new FeaturesRepository(prisma);

  // No teams in cal.diy, so canReadOthersBookings is always false.
  const canReadOthersBookings = false;

  const [bookingAuditEnabled, bookingsV3Enabled] = await Promise.all([
    featuresRepository.checkIfUserHasFeature(userId, "booking-audit"),
    featuresRepository.checkIfUserHasFeature(userId, "bookings-v3"),
  ]);

  return (
    <ShellMainAppDir
      {...(!bookingsV3Enabled
        ? {
            heading: t("bookings"),
            subtitle: t("bookings_description"),
          }
        : {})}>
      <BookingsList
        status={parsed.data.status}
        userId={userId}
        permissions={{ canReadOthersBookings }}
        bookingsV3Enabled={bookingsV3Enabled}
        bookingAuditEnabled={bookingAuditEnabled}
      />
    </ShellMainAppDir>
  );
};

export default Page;

import { prisma } from "@calcom/prisma";

import type { TGetBookingAttendeesInputSchema } from "./getBookingAttendees.schema";

type GetBookingAttendeesOptions = {
  ctx: Record<string, unknown>;
  input: TGetBookingAttendeesInputSchema;
};

export const getBookingAttendeesHandler = async ({ ctx: _ctx, input }: GetBookingAttendeesOptions) => {
  const bookingSeat = await prisma.bookingSeat.findUniqueOrThrow({
    where: {
      referenceUid: input.seatReferenceUid,
    },
    select: {
      booking: {
        select: {
          _count: {
            select: {
              seatsReferences: true,
            },
          },
        },
      },
    },
  });

  if (!bookingSeat) {
    throw new Error("Booking not found");
  }

  return bookingSeat.booking._count.seatsReferences;
};

import { ErrorWithCode } from "@calcom/lib/errors";
import type { EventTypeFavoriteRepository } from "../repositories/EventTypeFavoriteRepository";
import type { EventTypeRepository } from "../repositories/eventTypeRepository";

export interface IEventTypeFavoriteServiceDeps {
  eventTypeFavoriteRepository: EventTypeFavoriteRepository;
  eventTypeRepository: EventTypeRepository;
}

export type SetFavoriteInput = { userId: number; eventTypeId: number; isFavorite: boolean };

export class EventTypeFavoriteService {
  constructor(private readonly deps: IEventTypeFavoriteServiceDeps) {}

  async setFavorite({ userId, eventTypeId, isFavorite }: SetFavoriteInput): Promise<void> {
    // if unstarring, remove it right away.
    // no permission check is needed because you can only remove your own star
    if (!isFavorite) {
      await this.deps.eventTypeFavoriteRepository.delete({ userId, eventTypeId });
      return;
    }

    // make sure the event exists and the user is actually allowed to see it

    const hasAccess = await this.deps.eventTypeRepository.existsWithUserAccess({ id: eventTypeId, userId });
    // say "Not found" whether the event is missing or private
    if (!hasAccess) {
      throw ErrorWithCode.Factory.EventTypeNotFound(`Event type ${eventTypeId} not found`);
    }

    // save the star. If someone double-clicks quickly, it safely ignores the second click
    await this.deps.eventTypeFavoriteRepository.create({ userId, eventTypeId });
  }

  // gets the list of event IDs this user has starred, newest first
  async listFavoriteIds({ userId }: { userId: number }): Promise<number[]> {
    return this.deps.eventTypeFavoriteRepository.findEventTypeIdsByUserId(userId);
  }
}

import { useSearchParams, usePathname } from "next/navigation";
import { useMemo } from "react";

import { useLocale } from "@calcom/lib/hooks/useLocale";

export function useBookingStatusTab() {
  const { t } = useLocale();
  const searchParams = useSearchParams();
  const pathname = usePathname();

  const tabOptions = useMemo(() => {
    const queryString = searchParams?.toString() || "";

    const baseTabConfigs = [
      {
        value: "upcoming",
        label: "upcoming",
        path: "/bookings/upcoming",
        dataTestId: "upcoming",
      },
      {
        value: "unconfirmed",
        label: "unconfirmed",
        path: "/bookings/unconfirmed",
        dataTestId: "unconfirmed",
      },
      {
        value: "recurring",
        label: "recurring",
        path: "/bookings/recurring",
        dataTestId: "recurring",
      },
      {
        value: "past",
        label: "past",
        path: "/bookings/past",
        dataTestId: "past",
      },
      {
        value: "cancelled",
        label: "cancelled",
        path: "/bookings/cancelled",
        dataTestId: "cancelled",
      },
    ];

    return baseTabConfigs.map((tabConfig) => ({
      value: tabConfig.value,
      label: t(tabConfig.label),
      dataTestId: tabConfig.dataTestId,
      href: queryString ? `${tabConfig.path}?${queryString}` : tabConfig.path,
    }));
  }, [searchParams, t]);

  const currentTab = useMemo(() => {
    const pathMatch = pathname?.match(/\/bookings\/(\w+)/);
    return pathMatch?.[1] || "upcoming";
  }, [pathname]);

  return {
    currentTab,
    tabOptions,
  };
}

import { BookingStatus } from "@calcom/prisma/enums";
import type { AttendeeRepository } from "../repositories/AttendeeRepository";

export interface IBookingPeopleServiceDeps {
  attendeeRepository: AttendeeRepository;
}

export type BookingPersonDto = {
  name: string;
  email: string;
  meetingCount: number;
  lastMeetingAt: Date;
  // Event type of the most recent meeting, so "Book again" reopens the flow they last used
  lastEventType: { slug: string; teamSlug: string | null } | null;
};

export class BookingPeopleService {
  constructor(private readonly deps: IBookingPeopleServiceDeps) {}

  async listPeopleMet({
    userId,
    userEmail,
    now = new Date(),
  }: {
    userId: number;
    userEmail: string;
    now?: Date;
  }): Promise<BookingPersonDto[]> {
    // Only accepted bookings that already ended count as having "met" someone;
    // cancelled, rejected and still-pending bookings never happened
    const attendees = await this.deps.attendeeRepository.findByBookingUserIdIncludeBookingEventType({
      userId,
      bookingStatus: BookingStatus.ACCEPTED,
      bookingEndTimeBefore: now,
    });

    const ownEmail = userEmail.toLowerCase();
    const peopleByEmail = new Map<string, BookingPersonDto>();

    // Rows arrive newest first, so the first row seen for an email is their most recent meeting
    for (const attendee of attendees) {
      if (!attendee.booking) continue;

      // Emails are case-insensitive, and the same person is often typed differently across bookings
      const emailKey = attendee.email.toLowerCase();
      if (emailKey === ownEmail) continue;

      const existing = peopleByEmail.get(emailKey);
      if (existing) {
        existing.meetingCount += 1;
        continue;
      }

      const eventType = attendee.booking.eventType;
      peopleByEmail.set(emailKey, {
        name: attendee.name,
        email: attendee.email,
        meetingCount: 1,
        lastMeetingAt: attendee.booking.endTime,
        lastEventType: eventType ? { slug: eventType.slug, teamSlug: eventType.team?.slug ?? null } : null,
      });
    }

    return Array.from(peopleByEmail.values());
  }
}

```

import { createContainer } from "@calcom/features/di/di";

import { DI_TOKENS } from "@calcom/features/di/tokens";
import {
  type BookingPeopleService,
  moduleLoader as bookingPeopleServiceModuleLoader,
} from "./BookingPeopleService.module";

const bookingPeopleServiceContainer = createContainer();
// The Attendee repository module binds to PRISMA_CLIENT without loading Prisma itself
bookingPeopleServiceContainer.load(DI_TOKENS.PRISMA_MODULE, prismaModule);

export function getBookingPeopleService(): BookingPeopleService {
  bookingPeopleServiceModuleLoader.loadModule(bookingPeopleServiceContainer);
  return bookingPeopleServiceContainer.get<BookingPeopleService>(bookingPeopleServiceModuleLoader.token);
}

"use client";

import { useLocale } from "@calcom/lib/hooks/useLocale";
import { trpc } from "@calcom/trpc/react";
import useMeQuery from "@calcom/trpc/react/hooks/useMeQuery";
import { Button } from "@calcom/ui/components/button";
import { EmptyScreen } from "@calcom/ui/components/empty-screen";
import { ToggleGroup } from "@calcom/ui/components/form";
import { SkeletonText } from "@calcom/ui/components/skeleton";
import { useRouter } from "next/navigation";
import { useBookingStatusTab } from "~/bookings/hooks/useBookingStatusTab";
import { buildBookAgainUrl } from "~/bookings/lib/buildBookAgainUrl";

export default function BookingsPeopleView() {
  const { t, i18n } = useLocale();
  const router = useRouter();
  const { currentTab, tabOptions } = useBookingStatusTab();
  const { data: me } = useMeQuery();
  const { data: people, isPending } = trpc.viewer.bookings.getPeople.useQuery();

  const dateFormatter = new Intl.DateTimeFormat(i18n.language, { dateStyle: "medium" });

  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col gap-4">
      <div className="overflow-x-auto md:overflow-visible">
        <ToggleGroup
          value={currentTab}
          onValueChange={(value) => {
            const selectedTab = tabOptions.find((tab) => tab.value === value);
            if (selectedTab?.href) router.push(selectedTab.href);
          }}
          options={tabOptions}
        />
      </div>

      {isPending ? (
        <div className="flex flex-col gap-2">
          <SkeletonText className="h-12 w-full" />
          <SkeletonText className="h-12 w-full" />
          <SkeletonText className="h-12 w-full" />
        </div>
      ) : !people?.length ? (
        <EmptyScreen
          Icon="users"
          headline={t("no_people_yet")}
          description={t("no_people_yet_description")}
        />
      ) : (
        <ul className="border-subtle divide-subtle divide-y rounded-md border" data-testid="people-list">
          {people.map((person) => {
            const bookAgainUrl = buildBookAgainUrl({
              eventType: person.lastEventType
                ? { slug: person.lastEventType.slug, team: { slug: person.lastEventType.teamSlug } }
                : null,
              username: me?.username,
              attendee: { name: person.name, email: person.email },
            });

            return (
              <li
                key={person.email.toLowerCase()}
                className="flex flex-wrap items-center justify-between gap-3 px-4 py-3"
                data-testid="people-list-item">
                <div className="min-w-0">
                  <p className="text-emphasis truncate text-sm font-semibold">
                    {person.name || person.email}
                  </p>
                  <p className="text-subtle truncate text-sm">{person.email}</p>
                </div>
                <div className="flex items-center gap-4">
                  <div className="text-subtle text-right text-sm">
                    <p>{t("meeting_count", { count: person.meetingCount })}</p>
                    <p>
                      {t("last_met_on", { date: dateFormatter.format(new Date(person.lastMeetingAt)) })}
                    </p>
                  </div>
                  {bookAgainUrl ? (
                    <Button color="secondary" StartIcon="repeat" href={bookAgainUrl}>
                      {t("book_again")}
                    </Button>
                  ) : (
                    <Button color="secondary" StartIcon="repeat" disabled>
                      {t("book_again")}
                    </Button>
                  )}
                </div>
              </li>
            );
          })}
        </ul>
      )}
    </div>
  );
}

```

export const generateMetadata = async () =>
  await _generateMetadata(
    (t) => t("people"),
    (t) => t("people_description"),
    undefined,
    undefined,
    "/bookings/people"
  );

const Page = async () => {
  const session = await getServerSession({ req: buildLegacyRequest(await headers(), await cookies()) });
  if (!session?.user?.id) {
    return redirect("/auth/login");
  }

  const t = await getTranslate();

  return (
    <ShellMainAppDir heading={t("people")} subtitle={t("people_description")}>
      <BookingsPeopleView />
    </ShellMainAppDir>
  );
};

export default Page;

import { BookingStatus } from "@calcom/prisma/enums";
import { describe, expect, it, vi } from "vitest";
import type { AttendeeRepository } from "../repositories/AttendeeRepository";
import { BookingPeopleService } from "./BookingPeopleService";

type AttendeeRow = Awaited<ReturnType<AttendeeRepository["findByBookingUserIdIncludeBookingEventType"]>>[number];

function row({
  name,
  email,
  endTime,
  slug = "30min",
  teamSlug = null,
}: {
  name: string;
  email: string;
  endTime: string;
  slug?: string;
  teamSlug?: string | null;
}): AttendeeRow {
  return {
    name,
    email,
    booking: {
      endTime: new Date(endTime),
      eventType: { slug, team: teamSlug ? { slug: teamSlug } : null },
    },
  };
}

function setup(rows: AttendeeRow[]) {
  const attendeeRepository = {
    findByBookingUserIdIncludeBookingEventType: vi.fn().mockResolvedValue(rows),
  } as unknown as AttendeeRepository;
  const service = new BookingPeopleService({ attendeeRepository });
  return { service, attendeeRepository };
}

const now = new Date("2026-10-08T12:00:00Z");
const organizer = { userId: 1, userEmail: "host@example.com", now };

describe("BookingPeopleService", () => {
  describe("listPeopleMet", () => {
    it("only asks for accepted bookings that have already ended", async () => {
      const { service, attendeeRepository } = setup([]);

      await service.listPeopleMet(organizer);

      expect(attendeeRepository.findByBookingUserIdIncludeBookingEventType).toHaveBeenCalledWith({
        userId: 1,
        bookingStatus: BookingStatus.ACCEPTED,
        bookingEndTimeBefore: now,
      });
    });

    it("returns an empty list when there are no previous attendees", async () => {
      const { service } = setup([]);

      await expect(service.listPeopleMet(organizer)).resolves.toEqual([]);
    });

    it("lists each attendee once with their meeting count and most recent meeting", async () => {
      const { service } = setup([
        row({ name: "Ana", email: "ana@example.com", endTime: "2026-10-01T10:30:00Z", slug: "1on1" }),
        row({ name: "Ben", email: "ben@example.com", endTime: "2026-09-20T10:30:00Z" }),
        row({ name: "Ana", email: "ana@example.com", endTime: "2026-09-01T10:30:00Z", slug: "intro" }),
        row({ name: "Ana", email: "ana@example.com", endTime: "2026-08-01T10:30:00Z", slug: "intro" }),
      ]);

      const people = await service.listPeopleMet(organizer);

      expect(people).toEqual([
        {
          name: "Ana",
          email: "ana@example.com",
          meetingCount: 3,
          lastMeetingAt: new Date("2026-10-01T10:30:00Z"),
          lastEventType: { slug: "1on1", teamSlug: null },
        },
        {
          name: "Ben",
          email: "ben@example.com",
          meetingCount: 1,
          lastMeetingAt: new Date("2026-09-20T10:30:00Z"),
          lastEventType: { slug: "30min", teamSlug: null },
        },
      ]);
    });

    it("treats emails that differ only in case as the same person", async () => {
      const { service } = setup([
        row({ name: "Ana Lopez", email: "Ana@Example.com", endTime: "2026-10-01T10:30:00Z" }),
        row({ name: "Ana", email: "ana@example.com", endTime: "2026-09-01T10:30:00Z" }),
      ]);

      const people = await service.listPeopleMet(organizer);

      expect(people).toHaveLength(1);
      expect(people[0]).toMatchObject({ name: "Ana Lopez", email: "Ana@Example.com", meetingCount: 2 });
    });

    it("leaves out the organizer when they are also listed as an attendee", async () => {
      const { service } = setup([
        row({ name: "Host", email: "HOST@example.com", endTime: "2026-10-01T10:30:00Z" }),
        row({ name: "Ana", email: "ana@example.com", endTime: "2026-10-01T10:30:00Z" }),
      ]);

      const people = await service.listPeopleMet(organizer);

      expect(people.map((person) => person.email)).toEqual(["ana@example.com"]);
    });

    it("keeps the team slug of the most recent event type for team bookings", async () => {
      const { service } = setup([
        row({ name: "Ana", email: "ana@example.com", endTime: "2026-10-01T10:30:00Z", teamSlug: "sales" }),
      ]);

      const [person] = await service.listPeopleMet(organizer);

      expect(person.lastEventType).toEqual({ slug: "30min", teamSlug: "sales" });
    });

    it("returns a null event type when the last booking's event type was deleted", async () => {
      const { service } = setup([
        {
          name: "Ana",
          email: "ana@example.com",
          booking: { endTime: new Date("2026-10-01T10:30:00Z"), eventType: null },
        },
      ]);

      const [person] = await service.listPeopleMet(organizer);

      expect(person.lastEventType).toBeNull();
    });

    it("skips attendees that are no longer attached to a booking", async () => {
      const { service } = setup([{ name: "Ana", email: "ana@example.com", booking: null }]);

      await expect(service.listPeopleMet(organizer)).resolves.toEqual([]);
    });
  });
});

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-09 03:53:33Z)**_

The People view (#88) is written, and its tests pass (14/14, including #87's URL tests). The full `yarn type-check:ci --force` is still running in the background, so I don't know yet whether it passes. I'll report back when it finishes.

All changes are on a new branch, `feat/issue-88-people-view`, which starts from your #87 branch. I removed its upstream tracking so a push won't land on #87's branch. Nothing is committed.

**What it does**
- **People tab:** a new "People" tab sits next to Upcoming / Past / Cancelled and opens its own page at `/bookings/people`.
- **One row per person:** shows name, email, number of meetings, and the date you last met. The same person appears only once even if their email was typed with different capitals across bookings.
- **What counts as a meeting:** only accepted bookings that have already ended. You're left out of the list if you're also an attendee on your own booking.
- **Book again:** reuses `buildBookAgainUrl` from #87 and opens the event type you last met them on. The button is disabled if that event type has since been deleted.
- **Empty state:** shows a message when there's no one to list yet.

**Files**
- **Repository:** a new `findByBookingUserIdIncludeBookingEventType` method in `AttendeeRepository.ts`. It only selects the fields it needs and runs on an existing `[userId, endTime]` index.
- **Service:** `BookingPeopleService.ts` does the grouping, wired up with the same DI module/container pattern as the favorites feature, plus two new entries in `tokens.ts`.
- **tRPC:** a `viewer.bookings.getPeople` query (`getPeople.handler.ts`, plus an entry in `_router.tsx`).
- **UI:** `bookings-people-view.tsx`, `bookings/people/page.tsx` (the login check is here), and the new tab in `useBookingStatusTab.ts`.
- **Translations:** 6 new strings in `common.json`.
- **Tests:** `BookingPeopleService.test.ts` (8 tests) covers grouping, meeting counts, most recent date, case-insensitive emails, leaving you out, and the empty case.

**Things to know before you open the PR**
- **Size:** the PR has 11 code files, one over the guideline of 10, though the diff is small. The DI module and container add two files, but they follow the team's existing pattern.
- **Grouping happens after loading:** the database returns one row per past meeting and the service merges them into people. It's easy to test and fast enough, but someone with thousands of past meetings would load all those rows. If a reviewer pushes back, the merge can move into the SQL query.
- **The output type lives in the service file** rather than `packages/lib/dto/`, to keep the file count down. A reviewer may point that out.
- **I haven't opened the page in a running app**, so the layout hasn't been checked by eye.

Once the type check finishes, you can commit and open the PR yourself. In the description, put "Depends on #94" and "Part of #51". Until #94 merges, the PR will also show #87's commit.

+export default function BookingsPeopleView() {
+  const { t, i18n } = useLocale();
+  const router = useRouter();
+  const { currentTab, tabOptions } = useBookingStatusTab();
+  const { data: me } = useMeQuery();
+  const { data: people, isPending } = trpc.viewer.bookings.getPeople.useQuery();
+
+  const dateFormatter = new Intl.DateTimeFormat(i18n.language, { dateStyle: "medium" });
+
+  return (
+    <div className="flex flex-col gap-4">
+      <div className="overflow-x-auto md:overflow-visible">
+        <ToggleGroup
+          value={currentTab}
+          onValueChange={(value) => {
+            const selectedTab = tabOptions.find((tab) => tab.value === value);
+            if (selectedTab?.href) router.push(selectedTab.href);
+          }}
+          options={tabOptions}
+        />
+      </div>
+
+      {isPending ? (
+        <div className="flex flex-col gap-2">
+          <SkeletonText className="h-12 w-full" />
+          <SkeletonText className="h-12 w-full" />
+          <SkeletonText className="h-12 w-full" />
+        </div>
+      ) : !people?.length ? (
+        <EmptyScreen
+          Icon="users"
+          headline={t("no_people_yet")}
+          description={t("no_people_yet_description")}
+        />
+      ) : (
+        <ul className="border-subtle divide-subtle divide-y rounded-md border" data-testid="people-list">
+          {people.map((person) => {
+            const bookAgainUrl = buildBookAgainUrl({
+              eventType: person.lastEventType
+                ? { slug: person.lastEventType.slug, team: { slug: person.lastEventType.teamSlug } }
+                : null,
+              username: me?.username,
+              attendee: { name: person.name, email: person.email },
+            });
+
+            return (
+              <li
+                key={person.email.toLowerCase()}
+                className="flex flex-wrap items-center justify-between gap-3 px-4 py-3"
+                data-testid="people-list-item">
+                <div className="min-w-0">
+                  <p className="text-emphasis truncate text-sm font-semibold">
+                    {person.name || person.email}
+                  </p>
+                  <p className="text-subtle truncate text-sm">{person.email}</p>
+                </div>
+                <div className="flex items-center gap-4">
+                  <div className="text-subtle text-right text-sm">
+                    <p>{t("meeting_count", { count: person.meetingCount })}</p>
+                    <p>{t("last_met_on", { date: dateFormatter.format(new Date(person.lastMeetingAt)) })}</p>
+                  </div>
+                  {bookAgainUrl ? (
+                    <Button color="secondary" StartIcon="repeat" href={bookAgainUrl}>
+                      {t("book_again")}
+                    </Button>
+                  ) : (
+                    <Button color="secondary" StartIcon="repeat" disabled>
+                      {t("book_again")}
+                    </Button>
+                  )}
+                </div>
+              </li>
+            );
+          })}
+        </ul>
+      )}
+    </div>
+  );
+}

import { BookingStatus } from "@calcom/prisma/enums";
import type { AttendeeRepository } from "../repositories/AttendeeRepository";

export interface IBookingPeopleServiceDeps {
  attendeeRepository: AttendeeRepository;
}

export type BookingPersonDto = {
  name: string;
  email: string;
  meetingCount: number;
  lastMeetingAt: Date;
  // Event type of the most recent meeting, so "Book again" reopens the flow they last used
  lastEventType: { slug: string; teamSlug: string | null } | null;
};

export class BookingPeopleService {
  constructor(private readonly deps: IBookingPeopleServiceDeps) {}

  async listPeopleMet({
    userId,
    userEmail,
    now = new Date(),
  }: {
    userId: number;
    userEmail: string;
    now?: Date;
  }): Promise<BookingPersonDto[]> {
    // Only accepted bookings that already ended count as having "met" someone;
    // cancelled, rejected and still-pending bookings never happened
    const attendees = await this.deps.attendeeRepository.findByBookingUserIdIncludeBookingEventType({
      userId,
      bookingStatus: BookingStatus.ACCEPTED,
      bookingEndTimeBefore: now,
    });

    const ownEmail = userEmail.toLowerCase();
    const peopleByEmail = new Map<string, BookingPersonDto>();

    // Rows arrive newest first, so the first row seen for an email is their most recent meeting
    for (const attendee of attendees) {
      if (!attendee.booking) continue;

      // Emails are case-insensitive, and the same person is often typed differently across bookings
      const emailKey = attendee.email.toLowerCase();
      if (emailKey === ownEmail) continue;

      const existing = peopleByEmail.get(emailKey);
      if (existing) {
        existing.meetingCount += 1;
        continue;
      }

      const eventType = attendee.booking.eventType;
      peopleByEmail.set(emailKey, {
        name: attendee.name,
        email: attendee.email,
        meetingCount: 1,
        lastMeetingAt: attendee.booking.endTime,
        lastEventType: eventType ? { slug: eventType.slug, teamSlug: eventType.team?.slug ?? null } : null,
      });
    }

    return Array.from(peopleByEmail.values());
  }
}

### New files

**`BookingPeopleService.ts`** groups past attendees into one row per person.
```ts
async listPeopleMet({ userId, userEmail, now = new Date() }) {
  const attendees = await this.deps.attendeeRepository.findByBookingUserIdIncludeBookingEventType({
    userId, bookingStatus: BookingStatus.ACCEPTED, bookingEndTimeBefore: now,
  });
  const ownEmail = userEmail.toLowerCase();
  const peopleByEmail = new Map<string, BookingPersonDto>();

  // Rows arrive newest first, so the first row seen for an email is their most recent meeting
  for (const attendee of attendees) {
    if (!attendee.booking) continue;
    const emailKey = attendee.email.toLowerCase();
    if (emailKey === ownEmail) continue;

    const existing = peopleByEmail.get(emailKey);
    if (existing) { existing.meetingCount += 1; continue; }

    peopleByEmail.set(emailKey, {
      name: attendee.name, email: attendee.email, meetingCount: 1,
      lastMeetingAt: attendee.booking.endTime,
      lastEventType: eventType ? { slug: eventType.slug, teamSlug: eventType.team?.slug ?? null } : null,
    });
  }
  return Array.from(peopleByEmail.values());
}
```
